toyota.name: Toyota
toyota.description: Toyota is the world's largest automaker by volume, renowned for reliability and resale value. Founded in Japan, Toyota pioneered hybrid technology with the Prius and continues to lead in quality and durability. The brand offers everything from economical sedans to rugged trucks and luxury vehicles through its Lexus division.

honda.name: Honda
honda.description: Honda is one of the most trusted automotive brands in America, known for engineering excellence and long-term reliability. The Civic and Accord are perennial best-sellers that set the standard for compact and midsize sedans. Honda also produces motorcycles, power equipment, and aircraft.

ford.name: Ford
ford.description: Ford Motor Company is an American icon and the creator of the modern assembly line. The F-150 has been America's best-selling truck for over four decades, and the Mustang is one of the most recognized sports cars in history. Ford is aggressively expanding into electric vehicles with the Mustang Mach-E and F-150 Lightning.

chevrolet.name: Chevrolet
chevrolet.description: Chevrolet is one of America's most popular and enduring automotive brands, offering a full lineup from compact cars to heavy-duty trucks. The Silverado competes head-to-head with Ford's F-150, while the Corvette is an American performance legend. Chevrolet is a division of General Motors and sells vehicles in over 100 countries.

bmw.name: BMW
bmw.description: BMW, short for Bayerische Motoren Werke, is a German luxury automaker synonymous with driving pleasure and precision engineering. The brand's tagline 'The Ultimate Driving Machine' reflects its commitment to performance-oriented luxury vehicles. BMW offers a complete range of sedans, SUVs, coupes, and an expanding lineup of electric i-series models.

mercedes-benz.name: Mercedes-Benz
mercedes-benz.description: Mercedes-Benz is the world's oldest automotive brand, tracing its lineage to Karl Benz's 1886 Patent-Motorwagen. Known for cutting-edge technology, safety innovations, and refined luxury, Mercedes sets the standard for premium automobiles. The brand spans from entry-level luxury to ultra-premium Maybach models and high-performance AMG variants.

audi.name: Audi
audi.description: Audi is a German luxury automaker owned by the Volkswagen Group, known for its quattro all-wheel-drive system and progressive design language. The brand combines cutting-edge technology with understated elegance across its sedan and SUV lineups. Audi's e-tron electric vehicles represent the brand's push toward sustainable luxury mobility.

nissan.name: Nissan
nissan.description: Nissan is a Japanese automaker that offers a broad range of affordable and reliable vehicles for the American market. The Rogue is one of the best-selling SUVs in the country, and the Altima remains a popular midsize sedan. Nissan was an early pioneer in mass-market electric vehicles with the Leaf.

hyundai.name: Hyundai
hyundai.description: Hyundai has transformed from a budget brand into a formidable competitor offering exceptional value, technology, and design. The South Korean automaker backs its vehicles with one of the best warranties in the industry at 10 years or 100,000 miles on the powertrain. Hyundai's IONIQ sub-brand is rapidly expanding in the electric vehicle market.

kia.name: Kia
kia.description: Kia has undergone a dramatic brand transformation, evolving from a value brand into a design-forward automaker with award-winning vehicles. The Telluride has won numerous SUV of the Year awards, and the EV6 represents Kia's ambitious electric future. Kia offers a 10-year, 100,000-mile powertrain warranty, among the best in the industry.

volkswagen.name: Volkswagen
volkswagen.description: Volkswagen is one of the world's largest automakers, known for German engineering at accessible price points. The brand's name translates to 'People's Car,' reflecting its mission to offer quality vehicles for everyday drivers. VW is investing heavily in electrification with the ID series of electric vehicles.

subaru.name: Subaru
subaru.description: Subaru is known for its standard symmetrical all-wheel drive, boxer engines, and loyal customer base. The brand has a strong following among outdoor enthusiasts and is consistently ranked among the safest vehicles on the road. Subaru's commitment to safety and all-weather capability makes it especially popular in northern and mountainous states.

mazda.name: Mazda
mazda.description: Mazda is a Japanese automaker that prioritizes driving dynamics and design, often described as offering premium experiences at mainstream prices. The MX-5 Miata is the best-selling roadster in history, and the CX-5 is one of the top-rated compact SUVs. Mazda's Skyactiv technology focuses on efficiency without sacrificing performance.

lexus.name: Lexus
lexus.description: Lexus is Toyota's luxury division and has become synonymous with refined comfort, whisper-quiet cabins, and legendary reliability. The RX was one of the first luxury crossover SUVs and remains a segment leader. Lexus consistently tops customer satisfaction and dependability surveys.

acura.name: Acura
acura.description: Acura is Honda's luxury and performance division, offering precision-crafted vehicles with a sportier edge than many luxury competitors. The MDX is one of the best-selling three-row luxury SUVs in America. Acura combines Honda's renowned reliability with premium materials and advanced technology.

infiniti.name: Infiniti
infiniti.description: Infiniti is Nissan's luxury brand, offering a lineup of performance-inspired sedans and SUVs with distinctive design. The brand is known for powerful VQ-series engines and driver-focused interiors. Infiniti competes in the entry and mid-luxury segments against Lexus, Acura, and German rivals.

volvo.name: Volvo
volvo.description: Volvo is a Swedish luxury automaker with an unmatched reputation for safety innovation, having invented the three-point seatbelt in 1959. Now owned by Geely, Volvo combines Scandinavian minimalist design with cutting-edge safety technology. The brand has committed to becoming fully electric by 2030.

jeep.name: Jeep
jeep.description: Jeep is an iconic American brand synonymous with off-road capability and rugged adventure. The Wrangler traces its lineage to the World War II military vehicle and remains the gold standard for off-road SUVs. Jeep is a division of Stellantis and offers vehicles ranging from compact crossovers to full-size luxury SUVs.

ram.name: Ram
ram.description: Ram Trucks was spun off from Dodge in 2010 to create a dedicated truck brand under what is now Stellantis. The Ram 1500 is widely praised for its luxurious interior, smooth ride, and innovative features like the multifunction tailgate. Ram has rapidly gained market share in the fiercely competitive full-size truck segment.

dodge.name: Dodge
dodge.description: Dodge is an American performance brand known for muscle cars and powerful engines, especially the legendary Hemi V8. The Charger and Challenger are modern muscle car icons, and the Durango offers SUV practicality with performance credentials. Dodge is transitioning toward electrified performance under Stellantis.

chrysler.name: Chrysler
chrysler.description: Chrysler is one of America's oldest automotive brands, now operating as a smaller division within Stellantis. The Pacifica is widely regarded as the best minivan on the market, offering a plug-in hybrid option. Chrysler is being repositioned as a technology-forward brand with plans for full electrification.

buick.name: Buick
buick.description: Buick is a General Motors brand that bridges the gap between mainstream and luxury, offering quiet and comfortable vehicles at accessible prices. The brand is one of the oldest in America and has a massive following in China. Buick has shifted to an all-SUV lineup in the US market.

gmc.name: GMC
gmc.description: GMC is General Motors' premium truck and SUV brand, offering upscale versions of Chevrolet's truck lineup with distinctive styling and additional features. The Sierra and Yukon are among the most popular full-size trucks and SUVs in America. GMC revived the Hummer nameplate as an all-electric supertruck.

cadillac.name: Cadillac
cadillac.description: Cadillac is General Motors' luxury brand and was once the undisputed standard of the world in American luxury automobiles. The Escalade remains an icon of American luxury, and Cadillac is reinventing itself with the all-electric Lyriq. The brand competes with BMW, Mercedes-Benz, and Lexus in the premium market.

lincoln.name: Lincoln
lincoln.description: Lincoln is Ford's luxury division, known for serene interiors, smooth rides, and the iconic Navigator full-size SUV. The brand has undergone a significant renaissance with modern designs and the 'Quiet Flight' philosophy. Lincoln competes in the American luxury market against Cadillac, Lexus, and European imports.

tesla.name: Tesla
tesla.description: Tesla revolutionized the automotive industry by proving that electric vehicles could be desirable, high-performance, and practical for everyday use. The Model Y and Model 3 are among the best-selling vehicles in the world, and Tesla's Supercharger network is the largest fast-charging network in North America. Tesla also develops autonomous driving technology, energy storage, and solar products.

rivian.name: Rivian
rivian.description: Rivian is an American electric vehicle startup that launched with the R1T, the first electric pickup truck to reach production. The R1S is a three-row electric SUV that competes with luxury offerings from traditional automakers. Rivian also builds electric delivery vans for Amazon.

lucid.name: Lucid
lucid.description: Lucid Motors is an American electric vehicle manufacturer that produces the Lucid Air, an ultra-luxury EV sedan with industry-leading range. The Air Grand Touring achieved an EPA-estimated 516 miles of range, the highest of any EV. Lucid is backed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and is expanding into the SUV market with the Gravity.

porsche.name: Porsche
porsche.description: Porsche is a German sports car manufacturer and one of the most profitable automakers in the world. The 911 is one of the most iconic sports cars ever made, while the Cayenne and Macan SUVs drive the brand's sales volume. Porsche has successfully entered the electric market with the Taycan.

land-rover.name: Land Rover
land-rover.description: Land Rover is a British luxury SUV brand known for combining opulent interiors with genuine off-road capability. The Range Rover is the definitive luxury SUV and has been favored by royalty and celebrities for decades. Land Rover is owned by Tata Motors' Jaguar Land Rover division.

jaguar.name: Jaguar
jaguar.description: Jaguar is a British luxury automaker with a heritage rooted in elegant sports cars like the E-Type and XK series. The brand has expanded into SUVs with the F-Pace while maintaining its sporting character. Jaguar is transitioning to an all-electric luxury brand under Jaguar Land Rover.

mitsubishi.name: Mitsubishi
mitsubishi.description: Mitsubishi is a Japanese automaker now partnered with the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance, offering affordable SUVs and crossovers. The Outlander is available as a plug-in hybrid, one of the most affordable PHEVs on the market. Mitsubishi is known for value pricing and generous warranty coverage.

genesis.name: Genesis
genesis.description: Genesis is Hyundai's luxury brand that has rapidly established itself as a serious competitor to established German and Japanese luxury marques. The brand offers elegant design, advanced technology, and exceptional value compared to BMW and Mercedes-Benz. Genesis includes complimentary scheduled maintenance and valet service for owners.

alfa-romeo.name: Alfa Romeo
alfa-romeo.description: Alfa Romeo is an Italian luxury automaker with a storied racing heritage dating back over a century. The Giulia sedan and Stelvio SUV offer passionate Italian design and engaging driving dynamics. Alfa Romeo is part of Stellantis and is expanding its lineup with new electrified models.

fiat.name: Fiat
fiat.description: Fiat is Italy's largest automaker and one of the founding brands of Stellantis. The Fiat 500 is an iconic city car known for its retro charm and compact dimensions. Fiat's US presence has been scaled back significantly, with the brand focusing on the electrified 500e.

mini.name: Mini
mini.description: Mini is a British brand owned by BMW, known for its iconic compact cars with go-kart-like handling and distinctive retro-modern design. The Cooper is available in hardtop, convertible, and performance JCW variants. Mini is expanding into electric vehicles with the Cooper SE.

saab.name: Saab
saab.description: Saab was a Swedish automaker known for quirky engineering, turbocharged performance, and aviation-inspired design. The brand had a devoted following but ceased production in 2011 after bankruptcy. Saab vehicles were known for their unique ignition placement between the seats and strong safety record.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.description: Saturn was a General Motors brand created to compete with Japanese imports through a no-haggle pricing model and polymer body panels. The brand cultivated an enthusiastic owner community with annual 'Homecoming' events at its Spring Hill, Tennessee factory. Saturn was discontinued in 2010 during GM's bankruptcy restructuring.

pontiac.name: Pontiac
pontiac.description: Pontiac was General Motors' performance-oriented brand, famous for the GTO, Firebird, and Trans Am muscle cars. The brand's tagline 'We Build Excitement' captured its sporty image throughout the 1980s and 1990s. Pontiac was discontinued in 2010 as part of GM's bankruptcy restructuring.

oldsmobile.name: Oldsmobile
oldsmobile.description: Oldsmobile was one of America's oldest automotive brands and a cornerstone of General Motors for over a century. The Cutlass was America's best-selling car in the 1970s, and the 442 was a legendary muscle car. Oldsmobile was discontinued in 2004 after declining sales and brand identity challenges.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.description: Mercury was Ford's mid-level brand, positioned between Ford and Lincoln, offering slightly upscale versions of Ford vehicles. The Grand Marquis was a staple of taxi fleets and police departments, and the brand had a strong following among traditional American car buyers. Mercury was discontinued in 2011 as Ford streamlined its brand portfolio.

hummer.name: Hummer
hummer.description: Hummer was a brand of large SUVs and trucks derived from the military HMMWV (Humvee). The H2 became a cultural phenomenon in the early 2000s, symbolizing excess and off-road capability. The original Hummer brand was discontinued in 2010, but the nameplate was revived as a GMC sub-brand for an electric supertruck.

plymouth.name: Plymouth
plymouth.description: Plymouth was Chrysler's value brand, known for producing affordable vehicles and iconic muscle cars like the Barracuda and Road Runner. The Plymouth Voyager was one of the original minivans that created the segment in 1984. Plymouth was discontinued in 2001 as Chrysler consolidated its brand lineup.

scion.name: Scion
scion.description: Scion was Toyota's youth-oriented brand, designed to attract younger buyers with affordable, customizable vehicles and a no-haggle pricing model. The tC coupe and xB box car developed cult followings, and the FR-S sports car became a tuner favorite. Scion was discontinued in 2016, with its best models absorbed into the Toyota lineup.

suzuki.name: Suzuki
suzuki.description: Suzuki was a Japanese automaker known for small, affordable vehicles and the legendary Samurai compact SUV. The brand left the US automobile market in 2012 due to low sales volume, though it remains a major global automaker. Suzuki continues to sell motorcycles and ATVs in the United States.

isuzu.name: Isuzu
isuzu.description: Isuzu was known in the US market for rugged SUVs and trucks, particularly the Trooper and Rodeo. The brand exited the US consumer vehicle market in 2009 but continues to sell commercial trucks in North America. Isuzu remains one of the world's largest manufacturers of medium and heavy-duty diesel trucks.

smart.name: Smart
smart.description: Smart was a microcar brand created as a joint venture between Swatch and Mercedes-Benz, producing ultra-compact city cars. The ForTwo was the brand's signature model, measuring under nine feet long and perfect for urban parking. Smart exited the US market in 2019 but continues to sell electric vehicles in Europe and China.

polestar.name: Polestar
polestar.description: Polestar is a Swedish electric vehicle brand spun off from Volvo, focused on performance-oriented EVs with minimalist Scandinavian design. The Polestar 2 is a direct competitor to the Tesla Model 3, offering a refined driving experience and premium materials. Polestar is expanding its lineup with the Polestar 3 SUV and Polestar 4 coupe-SUV.

fisker.name: Fisker
fisker.description: Fisker was an American electric vehicle startup founded by Henrik Fisker, who previously created the Fisker Karma plug-in hybrid. The Fisker Ocean was a mid-size electric SUV that aimed to combine sustainability with accessible pricing. Fisker filed for bankruptcy in 2024 after production and distribution challenges.

lotus.name: Lotus
lotus.description: Lotus is a British sports car manufacturer renowned for lightweight engineering and exceptional handling, following founder Colin Chapman's philosophy of 'simplify, then add lightness.' The Emira is the brand's final internal combustion sports car, while the Eletre marks Lotus's entry into the electric SUV market. Lotus is now owned by Geely and is expanding globally.

maserati.name: Maserati
maserati.description: Maserati is an Italian luxury automaker with a rich racing heritage, known for its distinctive trident logo and sonorous engines. The brand offers grand touring cars and luxury SUVs that blend Italian craftsmanship with sporting character. Maserati is part of Stellantis and is electrifying its lineup with the Folgore range.

aston-martin.name: Aston Martin
aston-martin.description: Aston Martin is a British ultra-luxury sports car maker, famously associated with James Bond and British elegance. The brand produces hand-crafted grand tourers and the DBX luxury SUV at its Gaydon factory. Aston Martin combines bespoke craftsmanship with high performance in a very exclusive package.

bentley.name: Bentley
bentley.description: Bentley is a British ultra-luxury automaker owned by the Volkswagen Group, producing handcrafted vehicles at its Crewe factory in England. The Continental GT is the definitive modern grand tourer, and the Bentayga was the first ultra-luxury SUV. Bentley combines unmatched cabin opulence with surprising performance capabilities.

rolls-royce.name: Rolls-Royce
rolls-royce.description: Rolls-Royce is the pinnacle of automotive luxury, hand-building vehicles at its Goodwood factory with unparalleled attention to detail. Each Rolls-Royce takes months to complete and can be bespoke-ordered to virtually any specification. The brand, owned by BMW, has entered the electric era with the Spectre.

lamborghini.name: Lamborghini
lamborghini.description: Lamborghini is an Italian supercar manufacturer known for dramatic design, screaming engines, and outrageous performance. The Urus super-SUV has become the brand's best-selling model, making Lamborghini more accessible than ever. Lamborghini is owned by the Volkswagen Group through Audi and is transitioning to hybrid powertrains.

ferrari.name: Ferrari
ferrari.description: Ferrari is the world's most iconic sports car brand, synonymous with Formula 1 racing, Italian passion, and automotive excellence. The Prancing Horse badge represents decades of engineering innovation and racing victories. Ferrari deliberately limits production to maintain exclusivity and has become one of the most valuable luxury brands in the world.

mclaren.name: McLaren
mclaren.description: McLaren is a British supercar manufacturer born from the legendary McLaren Formula 1 team. The brand produces lightweight, carbon-fiber supercars that emphasize driver engagement and technological innovation. McLaren's road cars share engineering DNA with its F1 race cars, using carbon fiber tubs and advanced aerodynamics.

bugatti.name: Bugatti
bugatti.description: Bugatti is a French hyper-luxury automaker that produces the fastest and most expensive production cars in the world. The Chiron and its variants can exceed 300 mph, representing the absolute pinnacle of automotive engineering. Bugatti is now part of Bugatti Rimac, a joint venture between Porsche and Croatian EV maker Rimac.

maybach.name: Maybach
maybach.description: Maybach is Mercedes-Benz's ultra-luxury sub-brand, revived in 2015 as Mercedes-Maybach after the standalone brand was discontinued in 2012. The Mercedes-Maybach S-Class represents the pinnacle of luxury sedan motoring, competing with Rolls-Royce and Bentley. Maybach models feature exclusive design elements, premium materials, and extended wheelbases for rear-seat comfort.

delorean.name: DeLorean
delorean.description: DeLorean Motor Company produced the iconic DMC-12, a stainless steel sports car with gull-wing doors that became a pop culture legend through the Back to the Future films. The original company produced fewer than 9,000 cars before going bankrupt in 1982. A new DeLorean Motor Company has announced plans for an electric vehicle revival.

alabama.name: Alabama
alabama.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
alabama.lemonLawSummary: Alabama's Lemon Law covers new motor vehicles that develop substantial defects within the first year or 12,000 miles. Manufacturers must be given a reasonable number of repair attempts before a refund or replacement is required.
alabama.registrationNotes: Alabama charges a flat registration fee plus additional county-level taxes. Title fees are $18. Plates must be renewed annually by the owner's birthday.
alabama.description: Alabama requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles. The state has a lemon law that covers new vehicles purchased or leased in Alabama, and does not require emissions testing statewide.

alaska.name: Alaska
alaska.insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
alaska.lemonLawSummary: Alaska's Lemon Law protects buyers of new vehicles that have substantial defects. The manufacturer must be given a reasonable number of attempts to repair the defect before the consumer can seek a refund or replacement.
alaska.registrationNotes: Alaska charges a biennial registration fee of $100 for most passenger vehicles. There is no state sales tax, but some municipalities charge local taxes on vehicle purchases.
alaska.description: Alaska has some of the most unique vehicle ownership requirements in the nation. While liability insurance is mandatory, the state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections for most vehicles.

arizona.name: Arizona
arizona.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
arizona.lemonLawSummary: Arizona's Lemon Law requires manufacturers to repair defects within a reasonable number of attempts. If the vehicle remains defective, the buyer can request a replacement or refund through the state's arbitration program.
arizona.evIncentiveDetails: Arizona offers a reduced vehicle license tax for electric and alternative-fuel vehicles. EV owners also benefit from HOV lane access and some utility company charging incentives.
arizona.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in the Phoenix and Tucson metro areas for vehicles older than five model years. Vehicles are tested every other year. Testing costs approximately $17.
arizona.registrationFeeRange: $8 base fee plus vehicle license tax
arizona.registrationNotes: Arizona charges a low base registration fee of $8 but adds a vehicle license tax based on assessed value. New vehicles are assessed at 60% of MSRP, decreasing by 16.25% each year.
arizona.description: Arizona vehicle owners benefit from relatively low insurance minimums but must comply with emissions testing in the Phoenix and Tucson metro areas. The state offers incentives for electric and alternative fuel vehicles.

arkansas.name: Arkansas
arkansas.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
arkansas.lemonLawSummary: Arkansas's New Motor Vehicle Quality Assurance Act covers vehicles with substantial defects reported within 24 months or 24,000 miles. The manufacturer gets a reasonable number of repair attempts before a buyback is required.
arkansas.registrationNotes: Arkansas registration fees are based on vehicle weight. An annual personal property tax is also assessed on vehicles. Title transfers cost $10.
arkansas.description: Arkansas requires liability insurance and has a lemon law protecting new vehicle buyers. The state does not mandate emissions testing but does require annual safety inspections in some counties.

california.name: California
california.insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage
california.lemonLawSummary: California's Song-Beverly Consumer Warranty Act is one of the strongest lemon laws in the nation. It covers new and used certified vehicles with manufacturer warranties. After two or more repair attempts for serious defects, or 30+ days out of service, buyers may be entitled to a refund or replacement.
california.evIncentiveDetails: California offers the Clean Vehicle Rebate Project (CVRP) with rebates up to $7,500 for eligible EVs. Additional perks include HOV lane access, reduced registration fees for zero-emission vehicles, and various utility company incentives for home charging installation.
california.emissionsDetails: California requires biennial smog checks for vehicles older than eight model years in most areas. The state sets its own emissions standards through CARB, which are stricter than federal standards. Testing typically costs $30-$70.
california.registrationNotes: California charges a base registration fee of $46, a vehicle license fee (0.65% of vehicle value), plus various surcharges. Total first-year costs for a new vehicle can exceed $400. Renewal is annual.
california.description: California has the most comprehensive vehicle regulations in the country, including strict emissions standards, generous EV incentives, and strong consumer protection laws including a robust lemon law.

colorado.name: Colorado
colorado.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
colorado.lemonLawSummary: Colorado's Lemon Law covers new motor vehicles that develop nonconformities within the first year. After four repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, the manufacturer must replace the vehicle or refund the purchase price.
colorado.evIncentiveDetails: Colorado offers one of the most generous state EV tax credits in the nation, up to $5,000 for new electric vehicles. Combined with the federal credit, Colorado buyers can save over $12,000. Additional perks include reduced registration fees and utility incentives.
colorado.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in the Denver-Boulder-Greeley-Fort Collins metro area for vehicles 4-11 model years old. Testing is performed at Air Care Colorado stations and costs approximately $25.
colorado.registrationNotes: Colorado registration fees are based on vehicle weight and taxable value. A specific ownership tax is assessed that decreases with vehicle age. Registration is annual, due on the owner's birth month.
colorado.description: Colorado combines mandatory liability insurance with emissions testing in the Denver metro area. The state is a leader in EV incentives, offering substantial tax credits for electric vehicle purchases.

connecticut.name: Connecticut
connecticut.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
connecticut.lemonLawSummary: Connecticut's Lemon Law covers new vehicles that develop defects within 2 years or 24,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30+ days out of service, buyers can request arbitration for a refund or replacement.
connecticut.evIncentiveDetails: Connecticut offers the CHEAPR rebate program with up to $2,250 for new battery electric vehicles and $750 for plug-in hybrids. Additional incentives for low-income residents are available.
connecticut.emissionsDetails: Biennial emissions testing is required for most vehicles registered in Connecticut. Testing follows the OBD-II protocol for vehicles 4+ model years old. Cost is approximately $20.
connecticut.registrationNotes: Connecticut charges a biennial registration fee of $80 for most passenger vehicles. A supplemental fee applies to vehicles with a value above $50,000. Title fee is $25.
connecticut.description: Connecticut requires emissions testing for most vehicles and has strong consumer protection laws. The state mandates relatively high insurance minimums compared to the national average.

delaware.name: Delaware
delaware.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
delaware.lemonLawSummary: Delaware's Lemon Law covers new vehicles with defects reported within the express warranty period. The manufacturer must be given a reasonable opportunity to repair before arbitration can be pursued.
delaware.emissionsDetails: Delaware requires biennial emissions testing for vehicles in New Castle County that are more than 4 model years old. Testing uses OBD-II diagnostics and costs approximately $20.
delaware.safetyInspectionDetails: Delaware requires biennial safety inspections for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, tires, lights, windshield, exhaust, and other safety systems. Cost is approximately $35-$50 at authorized inspection stations.
delaware.registrationNotes: Delaware charges a flat registration fee and a 4.25% document fee on the purchase price in lieu of sales tax. Title fee is $55. No state sales tax applies to vehicle purchases.
delaware.description: Delaware requires liability insurance and biennial vehicle inspections. The state has no sales tax on vehicle purchases, which can represent significant savings for car buyers.

florida.name: Florida
florida.insuranceMinimumDetail: $10,000 personal injury protection (PIP) / $10,000 property damage liability. Bodily injury liability is only required if the driver has had license or registration suspended.
florida.lemonLawSummary: Florida's Lemon Law covers new or demonstrator vehicles within 24 months of delivery. After three repair attempts for the same defect or 15+ cumulative days out of service, the buyer can seek arbitration for a full refund or replacement.
florida.registrationNotes: Florida registration fees are based on vehicle weight. An initial registration fee applies, plus a $225 new wheels fee for first-time registrations. Title fee is $77.25 including lien recording.
florida.description: Florida is a no-fault insurance state, meaning your own insurance covers your injuries regardless of who caused the accident. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections.

georgia.name: Georgia
georgia.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
georgia.lemonLawSummary: Georgia's Lemon Law covers new vehicles that develop defects within the first 24 months or 24,000 miles. After three repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the buyer may be entitled to a replacement or refund.
georgia.evIncentiveDetails: Georgia has reinstated an alternative fuel vehicle tax credit program. Electric vehicle owners benefit from reduced charging costs through Georgia Power incentive programs and potential HOV lane access.
georgia.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in the 13-county metro Atlanta area for vehicles 3-25 model years old. Annual OBD-II testing costs $25 at Georgia Clean Air Force stations.
georgia.registrationNotes: Georgia charges a $20 annual registration fee plus a title ad valorem tax (TAVT) of 7% of the vehicle's fair market value at the time of purchase. This replaces the traditional annual ad valorem tax.
georgia.description: Georgia requires liability insurance and emissions testing in the metro Atlanta area. The state replaced its traditional sales tax on vehicles with a one-time title ad valorem tax (TAVT).

hawaii.name: Hawaii
hawaii.insuranceMinimumDetail: $20,000 bodily injury per person / $40,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $10,000 PIP
hawaii.lemonLawSummary: Hawaii's Lemon Law covers new vehicles with defects reported within the express warranty period or 2 years, whichever comes first. After three repair attempts or 30 days out of service, consumers may seek a refund or replacement.
hawaii.evIncentiveDetails: Hawaii offers EV rebates through its state energy office, reduced registration fees for electric vehicles, and access to HOV lanes. The state aims for 100% clean transportation by 2045.
hawaii.emissionsDetails: Oahu requires annual emissions inspections for gasoline-powered vehicles as part of the safety inspection process. Other islands only require safety inspections.
hawaii.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles in Hawaii. Inspections cover brakes, lights, tires, steering, and exhaust systems. Cost is typically $20-$30.
hawaii.registrationNotes: Hawaii charges a state registration fee plus a county-specific vehicle weight tax that varies by island. Registration is annual. Title fee is $5.
hawaii.description: Hawaii requires all registered vehicles to pass a periodic safety inspection. The state has mandatory no-fault insurance and offers growing incentives for electric vehicles as part of its clean energy goals.

idaho.name: Idaho
idaho.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
idaho.lemonLawSummary: Idaho's Lemon Law covers new motor vehicles with defects that substantially impair use, value, or safety. The manufacturer must be given a reasonable number of repair attempts within the warranty period.
idaho.registrationNotes: Idaho registration fees are based on the age of the vehicle, ranging from $69 for newer vehicles to $45 for those over 8 years old. An additional county fee and plate fee may apply.
idaho.description: Idaho has relatively low insurance requirements and does not mandate emissions testing or safety inspections for most personal vehicles. The state has a straightforward registration process.

illinois.name: Illinois
illinois.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
illinois.lemonLawSummary: Illinois's New Vehicle Buyer Protection Act covers vehicles in the first 12 months or 12,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, consumers can demand a replacement or refund.
illinois.evIncentiveDetails: Illinois offers EV rebates of up to $4,000 for new electric vehicles through the Illinois EPA. Additional rebates are available for charging equipment installation. Some utility companies offer discounted charging rates.
illinois.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in the greater Chicago area and Metro East St. Louis region for most vehicles 4-13 model years old. OBD-II testing is used, and testing costs $20.
illinois.registrationNotes: Illinois charges an annual registration fee of $151 for standard passenger vehicles. Electric vehicles pay an additional $100 annual fee. Title fee is $150.
illinois.description: Illinois requires liability insurance and emissions testing in the Chicago metro area and Metro East St. Louis. The state has a strong lemon law and offers incentives for electric vehicle purchases.

indiana.name: Indiana
indiana.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
indiana.lemonLawSummary: Indiana's Motor Vehicle Protection Act covers new vehicles within 18 months or 18,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, the consumer is entitled to a replacement or refund.
indiana.registrationNotes: Indiana charges a base registration fee of $21.35 plus an annual excise tax based on the vehicle's value and age. The excise tax decreases as the vehicle ages.
indiana.description: Indiana requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles and has a lemon law covering new car purchases. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections.

iowa.name: Iowa
iowa.insuranceMinimumDetail: $20,000 bodily injury per person / $40,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
iowa.lemonLawSummary: Iowa's Lemon Law protects purchasers of new vehicles that develop nonconformities within 2 years or 24,000 miles. After three repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the buyer may seek a refund or replacement.
iowa.registrationFeeRange: 1% of value annually, decreasing with age
iowa.registrationNotes: Iowa charges a fee-for-new-registration that is 5% of the purchase price, plus an annual registration fee based on the vehicle's book value (1% for the first year, decreasing to a minimum). Title fee is $25.
iowa.description: Iowa requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing but does have some of the most affordable vehicle registration fees in the nation.

kansas.name: Kansas
kansas.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
kansas.lemonLawSummary: Kansas's Lemon Law covers new vehicles with defects reported within the warranty period or 1 year, whichever is shorter. After four repair attempts or 30 days out of service, arbitration can be requested.
kansas.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in Johnson and Wyandotte counties (Kansas City metro area) for vehicles 4+ model years old. Biennial OBD-II testing costs approximately $17.
kansas.safetyInspectionDetails: Kansas requires a safety inspection when a vehicle is first registered in the state. Annual inspections are not required for most vehicles after initial registration.
kansas.registrationNotes: Kansas registration fees are based on vehicle weight. Personal property taxes are also assessed on vehicles. Registration is annual.
kansas.description: Kansas requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. Some counties in the Kansas City metro area require emissions testing. The state has a relatively straightforward registration process.

kentucky.name: Kentucky
kentucky.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
kentucky.lemonLawSummary: Kentucky's Lemon Law covers new vehicles with defects within the first 12 months or 12,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can request arbitration.
kentucky.registrationNotes: Kentucky charges a $21 annual registration fee for most passenger vehicles plus county clerk fees. A 6% usage tax applies to vehicle purchases. Personal property tax is assessed annually.
kentucky.description: Kentucky requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing but mandates personal property taxes on all vehicles.

louisiana.name: Louisiana
louisiana.insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
louisiana.lemonLawSummary: Louisiana's Lemon Law covers new vehicles with defects within the warranty period. After four repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can seek a refund or replacement through arbitration.
louisiana.safetyInspectionDetails: Louisiana requires an annual or biennial safety inspection for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, steering, lights, horn, mirrors, and tires. Cost is typically $10-$20.
louisiana.registrationNotes: Louisiana registration fees are based on the vehicle purchase price. Vehicles priced under $10,000 pay $20, while more expensive vehicles pay up to $82. License plate fees vary by parish.
louisiana.description: Louisiana requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state requires periodic safety inspections but does not mandate emissions testing statewide.

maine.name: Maine
maine.insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
maine.lemonLawSummary: Maine's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within 3 years or 18,000 miles. After three repair attempts or 15 business days out of service, the consumer can invoke arbitration for a refund or replacement.
maine.evIncentiveDetails: Maine offers the Efficiency Maine EV rebate program with incentives up to $2,000 for new battery electric vehicles. Low-income residents may qualify for enhanced rebates.
maine.emissionsDetails: Maine follows California's CARB emissions standards and requires OBD-II emissions testing in Cumberland County for vehicles older than the current plus one model year. Testing is annual.
maine.safetyInspectionDetails: Maine requires annual safety inspections for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, tires, lights, steering, exhaust, glass, and other safety components. Cost is typically $12.50.
maine.registrationNotes: Maine charges an annual registration fee based on vehicle weight, typically $35 for most passenger vehicles. Excise tax is also assessed based on the vehicle's MSRP and age.
maine.description: Maine requires liability insurance and annual vehicle inspections. The state has a strong lemon law and participates in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, promoting cleaner transportation.

maryland.name: Maryland
maryland.insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
maryland.lemonLawSummary: Maryland's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within 15 months or 15,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the manufacturer must accept the vehicle for arbitration. The law also covers used vehicles through the Used Vehicle Warranty Enforcement Act.
maryland.evIncentiveDetails: Maryland offers an excise tax credit of up to $3,000 for qualifying electric vehicles. The state also provides rebates for EV charging equipment installation and offers reduced tolls for EV owners.
maryland.emissionsDetails: Maryland requires biennial emissions testing in most counties for vehicles 4+ model years old using OBD-II testing. The Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP) test is free at state-operated stations.
maryland.safetyInspectionDetails: Maryland requires a safety inspection when a vehicle is sold or changes ownership. The inspection covers major safety systems. Cost varies by inspection station, typically $60-$100.
maryland.registrationNotes: Maryland charges a biennial registration fee based on vehicle weight. The state also charges a 6% excise tax on vehicle purchases. Title fee is $100.
maryland.description: Maryland requires liability insurance, safety inspections for vehicle transfers, and has a strong lemon law. The state mandates emissions testing and offers growing EV incentive programs.

massachusetts.name: Massachusetts
massachusetts.insuranceMinimumDetail: $20,000 bodily injury per person / $40,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage
massachusetts.lemonLawSummary: Massachusetts's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the first year or 15,000 miles. After three repair attempts or 15 business days out of service, the consumer can invoke the law. The state also has strong used car warranty protections.
massachusetts.evIncentiveDetails: Massachusetts offers MOR-EV rebates of up to $3,500 for new battery electric vehicles. Additional incentives include reduced registration fees, HOV lane access, and utility-sponsored charging programs.
massachusetts.emissionsDetails: Massachusetts requires annual emissions testing as part of the combined safety and emissions inspection for vehicles older than the current plus one model year. OBD-II testing is used.
massachusetts.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual combined safety and emissions inspections are required for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, tires, lights, windshield, exhaust, and OBD-II emissions. Cost is $35.
massachusetts.registrationNotes: Massachusetts charges a $60 biennial registration fee for most passenger vehicles. A 6.25% sales tax applies to vehicle purchases. Title fee is $75.
massachusetts.description: Massachusetts requires annual vehicle inspections that include both safety and emissions components. The state has strong consumer protections and significant EV incentive programs.

michigan.name: Michigan
michigan.insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / PIP coverage required
michigan.lemonLawSummary: Michigan's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period. After four repair attempts for the same defect or 30 days out of service, the consumer can request arbitration. Michigan also uniquely allows claims for used vehicles under certain conditions.
michigan.evIncentiveDetails: Michigan offers incentives through its Charge Up Michigan program and various utility company rebates for home charging station installation. The state is also investing heavily in EV infrastructure.
michigan.registrationNotes: Michigan registration fees are based on the vehicle's list price (MSRP). Fees range from $100 for vehicles with an MSRP below $6,000 to over $200 for more expensive vehicles. No annual property tax on vehicles.
michigan.description: Michigan is a no-fault insurance state with unique auto insurance requirements. As the heart of the American auto industry, the state has comprehensive vehicle laws and strong consumer protections.

minnesota.name: Minnesota
minnesota.insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $40,000 PIP
minnesota.lemonLawSummary: Minnesota's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period or 2 years, whichever comes first. After four repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, the consumer may seek a refund or replacement.
minnesota.evIncentiveDetails: Minnesota offers rebates of up to $2,500 for battery electric vehicle purchases through its Clean Cars Minnesota initiative. Utility incentives for home charging are also available.
minnesota.emissionsDetails: Minnesota requires emissions testing in the seven-county Twin Cities metro area for most vehicles. Testing is performed at state-contracted stations. Newer vehicles and electric vehicles are exempt.
minnesota.registrationNotes: Minnesota charges a $35 base registration fee plus a registration tax based on the vehicle's value (1.285% of base value, which decreases with age). Title fee is $8.25.
minnesota.description: Minnesota requires liability insurance and has a no-fault insurance component. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and offers growing incentives for EV adoption.

mississippi.name: Mississippi
mississippi.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
mississippi.lemonLawSummary: Mississippi's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the first year or 12,000 miles. After three repair attempts or 15 business days out of service, the consumer can pursue arbitration for a refund or replacement.
mississippi.registrationNotes: Mississippi has some of the lowest registration fees in the nation. Fees range from $12.75 for vehicles under 6,500 lbs to $24.75 for larger vehicles. A 5% use tax applies to vehicle purchases.
mississippi.description: Mississippi requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles and has a lemon law for new vehicle purchases. The state does not require emissions testing or annual safety inspections.

missouri.name: Missouri
missouri.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
missouri.lemonLawSummary: Missouri's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the first year or 12,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, the consumer can seek a refund or replacement.
missouri.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in the St. Louis and Kansas City metro areas for gasoline-powered vehicles from 2 to 25 model years old. Biennial OBD-II testing costs approximately $24.
missouri.safetyInspectionDetails: Missouri requires safety inspections every two years or when a vehicle changes ownership. Inspections cover brakes, lights, steering, tires, glass, and horn. Cost is typically $12.
missouri.registrationNotes: Missouri registration fees are uniquely based on vehicle horsepower. Fees range from $18.25 for vehicles under 12 hp to $51.25 for vehicles over 72 hp. Personal property tax is also assessed annually.
missouri.description: Missouri requires liability insurance and safety inspections. The state has emissions testing in the St. Louis and Kansas City metro areas and a lemon law protecting new vehicle buyers.

montana.name: Montana
montana.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
montana.lemonLawSummary: Montana's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within 2 years or 18,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, the consumer can seek a refund or replacement.
montana.registrationFeeRange: Based on vehicle age, typically $100-$300 for newer vehicles
montana.registrationNotes: Montana does not charge a sales tax on vehicle purchases, making it popular for out-of-state registrations. Registration fees are based on the vehicle's age, with newer vehicles paying more. A county option tax may also apply.
montana.description: Montana is popular for vehicle registration due to its lack of sales tax. The state requires liability insurance but does not mandate emissions testing or safety inspections for most vehicles.

nebraska.name: Nebraska
nebraska.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
nebraska.lemonLawSummary: Nebraska's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the manufacturer's express warranty period. After four repair attempts or 40 days out of service, the consumer may be entitled to a refund or replacement.
nebraska.registrationNotes: Nebraska charges a $15 registration fee plus a motor vehicle tax based on the vehicle's value and age. The tax decreases as the vehicle ages. Title fee is $10.
nebraska.description: Nebraska requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing and has a motor vehicle tax based on vehicle value.

nevada.name: Nevada
nevada.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
nevada.lemonLawSummary: Nevada's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the first year or 12,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30 calendar days out of service, the consumer can demand a replacement or refund.
nevada.evIncentiveDetails: Nevada offers a partial vehicle registration fee discount for electric vehicles and a property tax exemption for EV charging equipment. NV Energy offers home charging incentives.
nevada.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in Clark County (Las Vegas) and Washoe County (Reno) for vehicles of certain ages. Testing uses OBD-II for newer vehicles and costs approximately $21.
nevada.registrationNotes: Nevada charges a $33 registration fee plus a governmental services tax based on the vehicle's depreciated MSRP. Registration is annual. The state does not have a state income tax.
nevada.description: Nevada requires liability insurance and emissions testing in the Las Vegas and Reno metro areas. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and offers growing EV incentive programs.

new-hampshire.name: New Hampshire
new-hampshire.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage. Note: Insurance is not mandatory in New Hampshire, but these minimums apply if you carry coverage.
new-hampshire.lemonLawSummary: New Hampshire's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period. After three repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, the consumer can request arbitration.
new-hampshire.emissionsDetails: New Hampshire requires annual OBD-II emissions testing as part of the annual safety inspection for vehicles 2 or more model years old. Diesel vehicles are exempt.
new-hampshire.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, exhaust, lights, steering, tires, glass, and emissions (OBD-II). Cost is typically $25-$50.
new-hampshire.registrationNotes: New Hampshire registration fees are based on vehicle weight. A municipal permit fee based on vehicle value is also assessed by the town or city. No sales tax on vehicle purchases.
new-hampshire.description: New Hampshire is unique in that it does not require auto insurance by law, though drivers remain financially responsible for damages. The state mandates annual safety inspections.

new-jersey.name: New Jersey
new-jersey.insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage / $15,000 PIP
new-jersey.lemonLawSummary: New Jersey's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within 2 years or 24,000 miles. After three repair attempts or 20 days out of service, the consumer can seek a refund or replacement. The state also covers leased vehicles.
new-jersey.evIncentiveDetails: New Jersey exempts electric vehicles from sales tax and offers a Charge Up New Jersey rebate of up to $4,000 for new EV purchases. The state is also investing heavily in public charging infrastructure.
new-jersey.emissionsDetails: New Jersey requires biennial emissions inspections for most vehicles 5+ model years old. Testing is performed at state Motor Vehicle Commission inspection stations at no charge.
new-jersey.registrationNotes: New Jersey charges annual registration fees based on vehicle weight. A 6.625% sales tax applies to vehicle purchases (EVs are exempt). Title fee is $60.
new-jersey.description: New Jersey requires no-fault insurance with some of the highest minimum coverage requirements in the nation. The state mandates emissions testing and has strong consumer protection laws.

new-mexico.name: New Mexico
new-mexico.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
new-mexico.lemonLawSummary: New Mexico's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period or 1 year. After four repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, the consumer can seek a replacement or refund.
new-mexico.evIncentiveDetails: New Mexico offers a tax credit of up to $2,500 for the purchase of new alternative fuel vehicles. Additional incentives are available through local utilities for home charging installation.
new-mexico.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in Bernalillo County (Albuquerque) for most vehicles 2+ model years old. Biennial OBD-II testing is performed at authorized stations.
new-mexico.registrationNotes: New Mexico registration fees are based on vehicle year. Newer vehicles (0-2 years) pay $62, with fees decreasing to $27 for vehicles 7+ years old. Registration is annual.
new-mexico.description: New Mexico requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles. The state has emissions testing in the Albuquerque area and a lemon law covering new vehicle purchases.

new-york.name: New York
new-york.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $50,000 PIP (no-fault) required
new-york.lemonLawSummary: New York's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within 2 years or 18,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can seek a refund or replacement. New York also has a strong Used Car Lemon Law covering recent-model used vehicles.
new-york.evIncentiveDetails: New York offers the Drive Clean rebate of up to $2,000 for new EVs. Additional incentives include the EV Make-Ready program for charging infrastructure, Con Edison rebates for NYC-area EV owners, and HOV lane access.
new-york.emissionsDetails: Annual emissions testing is required statewide as part of the annual safety inspection for most vehicles 2+ model years old. OBD-II testing is used for 1996+ model year vehicles.
new-york.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, steering, tires, lights, glass, exhaust, and emissions. Cost varies by shop but is typically $10-$37.
new-york.registrationNotes: New York registration fees are based on vehicle weight, ranging from $26 to $140 for a biennial period. NYC residents also pay a supplemental registration fee. Sales tax varies by county.
new-york.description: New York has comprehensive vehicle ownership requirements including no-fault insurance, annual safety and emissions inspections, and one of the strongest lemon laws in the nation.

north-carolina.name: North Carolina
north-carolina.insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
north-carolina.lemonLawSummary: North Carolina's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within 24 months or 24,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 20 cumulative business days out of service, the consumer can seek a replacement or refund.
north-carolina.emissionsDetails: Annual emissions and safety inspections are required in 47 of 100 counties for vehicles 3-20 model years old. OBD-II testing is used and costs approximately $30.
north-carolina.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required statewide for all registered vehicles. In some counties, the inspection includes both safety and emissions components. Cost is approximately $13.60 for safety only.
north-carolina.registrationNotes: North Carolina charges a $38.75 annual registration fee for most vehicles. A 3% highway use tax (capped at $250) applies to vehicle purchases. Title fee is $56.
north-carolina.description: North Carolina requires liability insurance and annual safety and emissions inspections. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and collects a highway use tax on vehicle purchases.

north-dakota.name: North Dakota
north-dakota.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
north-dakota.lemonLawSummary: North Dakota's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the express warranty period or 1 year. After three repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, the consumer can seek a replacement or refund.
north-dakota.registrationNotes: North Dakota registration fees are based on vehicle weight and model year. Fees decrease as the vehicle ages. Annual renewal is required.
north-dakota.description: North Dakota requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections and has some of the lowest insurance rates in the nation.

ohio.name: Ohio
ohio.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
ohio.lemonLawSummary: Ohio's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within 1 year or 18,000 miles. After three repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can request arbitration for a refund or replacement.
ohio.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing (E-Check) is required in select urban counties including parts of greater Cleveland and greater Akron for vehicles 4-25 model years old. Testing is free at designated stations.
ohio.registrationNotes: Ohio charges a base registration fee of $31 plus a highway use tax and county-specific permissive taxes that vary. Electric vehicles pay an additional $200 annual fee. Title fee is $15.
ohio.description: Ohio requires liability insurance but is unique in that it uses a financial responsibility law rather than mandatory insurance. The state requires emissions testing in certain urban counties.

oklahoma.name: Oklahoma
oklahoma.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
oklahoma.lemonLawSummary: Oklahoma's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the first year or 12,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 45 days out of service, the consumer can seek a replacement or refund through arbitration.
oklahoma.registrationNotes: Oklahoma charges a registration fee based on the vehicle's age and original factory price. An excise tax of 1.25% of the purchase price or NADA book value applies for first-time registrations.
oklahoma.description: Oklahoma requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing but mandates personal property taxes on vehicles, known as excise tax.

oregon.name: Oregon
oregon.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
oregon.lemonLawSummary: Oregon's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period or 1 year. After four repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, the consumer can seek a replacement or refund.
oregon.evIncentiveDetails: Oregon offers the Clean Vehicle Rebate of up to $5,000 for new EVs and $2,500 for used EVs. Low-income buyers may qualify for an additional $2,500 rebate. The state also has no sales tax on any vehicle purchase.
oregon.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in the Portland metro area and Rogue Valley for vehicles 1975 and newer. DEQ testing is performed every two years and costs $21-$25.
oregon.registrationNotes: Oregon charges registration fees based on vehicle fuel type and MPG rating. Standard vehicles pay $122 for 2 years. Electric vehicles pay $306 for 2 years. No sales tax applies.
oregon.description: Oregon has no sales tax on vehicle purchases and requires emissions testing in the Portland metro area. The state has a strong lemon law and offers significant incentives for electric vehicles.

pennsylvania.name: Pennsylvania
pennsylvania.insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage
pennsylvania.lemonLawSummary: Pennsylvania's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the first year, warranty period, or 12,000 miles, whichever comes first. After three repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can invoke the law.
pennsylvania.evIncentiveDetails: Pennsylvania offers rebates through the Alternative Fuel Vehicle program and DCED grants for EV charging station installation. Some utility companies offer additional incentives for home charging.
pennsylvania.emissionsDetails: Annual emissions testing is required in 25 counties, including the Pittsburgh and Philadelphia metro areas. Testing follows OBD-II protocols for 1996+ model year vehicles. Cost is typically $34-$38.
pennsylvania.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, steering, suspension, tires, lights, glass, body, and chassis. Cost is typically $35-$50.
pennsylvania.registrationNotes: Pennsylvania charges a flat $38 annual registration fee for most passenger vehicles. A 6% sales tax applies to vehicle purchases. Title fee is $55.
pennsylvania.description: Pennsylvania requires liability insurance and annual safety and emissions inspections. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and is part of a multi-state emissions standards agreement.

rhode-island.name: Rhode Island
rhode-island.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
rhode-island.lemonLawSummary: Rhode Island's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within 1 year or 15,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can seek a refund or replacement.
rhode-island.evIncentiveDetails: Rhode Island offers the DRIVE EV rebate program with incentives up to $2,500 for new battery electric vehicles. The state also provides incentives for charging station installation.
rhode-island.emissionsDetails: Rhode Island requires biennial emissions inspections for all vehicles 2 or more model years old. OBD-II testing is used for 1996+ model year vehicles. Testing is performed at private stations.
rhode-island.safetyInspectionDetails: Biennial safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, tires, lights, steering, exhaust, glass, and wipers. Cost varies by station.
rhode-island.registrationNotes: Rhode Island charges a biennial registration fee of $30 for most vehicles. A 7% sales tax applies to vehicle purchases. Title fee is $52.50.
rhode-island.description: Rhode Island requires liability insurance and biennial safety and emissions inspections. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and eliminated the car excise tax in recent years.

south-carolina.name: South Carolina
south-carolina.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
south-carolina.lemonLawSummary: South Carolina's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period or 1 year. After three repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can request arbitration for a refund or replacement.
south-carolina.registrationNotes: South Carolina charges a $40 biennial registration fee for most vehicles. A 5% infrastructure maintenance fee (IMF) applies in lieu of sales tax, capped at $500. Personal property tax is also assessed.
south-carolina.description: South Carolina requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or annual safety inspections and has a low personal property tax on vehicles.

south-dakota.name: South Dakota
south-dakota.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
south-dakota.lemonLawSummary: South Dakota's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period. After four repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can seek a replacement or refund through arbitration.
south-dakota.registrationNotes: South Dakota charges registration fees based on vehicle weight and age. A 4% excise tax applies to all vehicle purchases. No annual personal property tax on vehicles.
south-dakota.description: South Dakota requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections and has no state income tax.

tennessee.name: Tennessee
tennessee.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
tennessee.lemonLawSummary: Tennessee's Motor Vehicle Warranty Enforcement Act covers new vehicles within the warranty period. After four repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can seek a replacement or refund.
tennessee.evIncentiveDetails: Tennessee offers incentives through TVA partnerships and local utility programs for EV charging station installation. The state is home to several EV manufacturing facilities and offers related tax incentives.
tennessee.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in Davidson, Hamilton, Rutherford, Sumner, Williamson, and Wilson counties for vehicles 3-25 model years old. Annual OBD-II testing costs $9.
tennessee.registrationNotes: Tennessee charges a flat $26.50 annual registration fee for most passenger vehicles. A state and local sales tax (typically 7-9.75%) applies to vehicle purchases. Title fee is $11.
tennessee.description: Tennessee requires liability insurance and has emissions testing in select metro counties. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and charges no state income tax on wages.

texas.name: Texas
texas.insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
texas.lemonLawSummary: Texas's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period or 24 months. After four repair attempts, two attempts for a serious safety defect, or 30 days out of service, the consumer can file a complaint with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles.
texas.evIncentiveDetails: Texas offers the Light-Duty Motor Vehicle Purchase or Lease Incentive Program with up to $2,500 for new EVs. Various utility companies offer additional rebates for home charging installation. Some cities offer additional local incentives.
texas.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required as part of the annual safety inspection in 17 urban counties including Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, Austin, San Antonio, and El Paso. Cost is approximately $11.50 for the emissions portion.
texas.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles in Texas. Inspections cover brakes, horn, lights, mirrors, steering, tires, exhaust, glass, and other safety systems. Cost is $7.50 for non-commercial vehicles.
texas.registrationNotes: Texas charges a base registration fee of $50.75 for most passenger vehicles. A 6.25% motor vehicle sales tax applies to purchases. Title fee is $33.
texas.description: Texas requires liability insurance and annual safety inspections. The state has emissions testing in select urban counties and is one of the largest vehicle markets in the country.

utah.name: Utah
utah.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $65,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage / $3,000 PIP
utah.lemonLawSummary: Utah's New Motor Vehicle Warranties Act covers new vehicles within the warranty period. After four repair attempts or 30 business days out of service, the consumer can seek a refund or replacement.
utah.evIncentiveDetails: Utah offers a Clean Fuel Vehicle tax credit and reduced registration fees for electric vehicles through certain years. Rocky Mountain Power offers incentives for EV charging station installation.
utah.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in Salt Lake, Davis, Utah, Weber, and Cache counties. Testing frequency varies by county and vehicle age (annual or biennial). OBD-II testing costs approximately $30.
utah.safetyInspectionDetails: Safety inspections are required annually for vehicles 10+ years old in most counties. Newer vehicles are exempt until they reach 4-8 years old, depending on county. Cost is approximately $30.
utah.registrationNotes: Utah charges registration fees based on vehicle age. Newer vehicles pay $69, with fees decreasing to $44 for vehicles 12+ years old. A uniform fee of $150 applies to all new vehicle registrations.
utah.description: Utah requires liability insurance and has emissions testing in several Wasatch Front counties. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and safety inspections based on vehicle age.

vermont.name: Vermont
vermont.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
vermont.lemonLawSummary: Vermont's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period or 2 years. After three repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can seek a refund or replacement through arbitration.
vermont.evIncentiveDetails: Vermont offers incentives through the Mileage Smart program, providing up to $5,000 in incentives for income-eligible residents purchasing efficient or electric vehicles. Additional utility incentives are available.
vermont.emissionsDetails: Annual OBD-II emissions testing is required as part of the annual safety inspection for vehicles 2+ model years old. Vermont follows California's vehicle emission standards (CARB).
vermont.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, steering, tires, lights, exhaust, glass, and OBD-II emissions. Cost is typically $35.
vermont.registrationNotes: Vermont charges an annual registration fee of $76 for most vehicles. A 6% purchase and use tax applies to vehicle purchases. Title fee is $35.
vermont.description: Vermont requires liability insurance and annual safety and emissions inspections. The state follows California emissions standards and offers incentives for electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles.

virginia.name: Virginia
virginia.insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
virginia.lemonLawSummary: Virginia's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within 18 months of purchase. After three repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can invoke the Virginia Motor Vehicle Warranty Enforcement Act.
virginia.evIncentiveDetails: Virginia offers a reduced rate for HOV lane tolling for qualifying clean fuel vehicles. Some utility companies offer rebates for home EV charging equipment. The state is investing in charging infrastructure through the VW settlement funds.
virginia.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in Northern Virginia and certain other localities as part of the annual safety inspection. OBD-II testing is used for 1996+ model year vehicles.
virginia.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles statewide. Inspections cover brakes, steering, suspension, tires, lights, glass, horn, exhaust, and mirrors. Cost is $20.
virginia.registrationNotes: Virginia charges annual registration fees based on vehicle weight. An annual personal property tax is also assessed by the locality, with partial state relief available. Title fee is $15.
virginia.description: Virginia requires liability insurance and annual safety inspections statewide. The state has emissions testing in Northern Virginia and has a lemon law protecting new vehicle buyers.

washington.name: Washington
washington.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
washington.lemonLawSummary: Washington's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within 24 months or 24,000 miles. After four repair attempts, two for a condition likely to cause death or serious injury, or 30 days out of service, the consumer can seek a refund or replacement.
washington.evIncentiveDetails: Washington exempts electric vehicles from state sales tax on the first $15,000 of the purchase price. The state also offers HOV lane access for EVs and is investing heavily in charging infrastructure.
washington.emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required in parts of Clark, King, Pierce, Snohomish, and Spokane counties for vehicles 5-25 model years old. Biennial OBD-II testing costs $15.
washington.registrationFeeRange: $30 base plus RTA tax in some areas
washington.registrationNotes: Washington charges a $30 base registration fee. In areas with regional transit authority (Sound Transit), an additional RTA excise tax of 1.1% of vehicle value applies. EV owners pay a $225 annual fee.
washington.description: Washington requires liability insurance and has emissions testing in certain areas. The state has no income tax, a strong lemon law, and significant incentives for electric vehicle adoption.

west-virginia.name: West Virginia
west-virginia.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
west-virginia.lemonLawSummary: West Virginia's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the first year or warranty period. After three repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can seek a refund or replacement.
west-virginia.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, steering, tires, lights, glass, exhaust, horn, and mirrors. Cost is typically $10-$19.
west-virginia.registrationNotes: West Virginia charges a $51.50 annual registration fee for most passenger vehicles. A 6% sales tax applies to vehicle purchases. Title fee is $15. Personal property tax is also assessed.
west-virginia.description: West Virginia requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing but mandates annual vehicle safety inspections.

wisconsin.name: Wisconsin
wisconsin.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
wisconsin.lemonLawSummary: Wisconsin's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period or 1 year. After four repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can seek a replacement or refund through the state's dispute resolution program.
wisconsin.registrationNotes: Wisconsin charges an $85 annual registration fee for most passenger vehicles. A 5% sales tax applies to vehicle purchases, plus a 0.5% county tax. Title fee is $164.50.
wisconsin.description: Wisconsin requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections for most personal vehicles.

wyoming.name: Wyoming
wyoming.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
wyoming.lemonLawSummary: Wyoming's Lemon Law covers new vehicles within the warranty period or 1 year. After three repair attempts or 30 days out of service, the consumer can seek a replacement or refund.
wyoming.registrationNotes: Wyoming charges registration fees based on the vehicle's fair market value and county mills. A 5% use tax applies to vehicle purchases. No state income tax.
wyoming.description: Wyoming requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections and has no state income tax.

washington-dc.name: Washington DC
washington-dc.insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
washington-dc.lemonLawSummary: Washington DC's Lemon Law covers new vehicles with substantial defects within 2 years or 18,000 miles. After four repair attempts or 30 cumulative days out of service, the consumer can demand a refund or replacement from the manufacturer.
washington-dc.evIncentiveDetails: Washington DC offers a reduced excise tax rate for electric vehicles, free residential parking permits for EVs, and access to an expanding public charging network. DC also participates in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative and offers rebates for home charging station installation.
washington-dc.emissionsDetails: DC requires biennial emissions inspections for most vehicles 4 or more model years old. OBD-II testing is performed at DC DMV inspection stations. Electric and hybrid vehicles may be exempt from testing.
washington-dc.safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles in DC. Inspections cover brakes, steering, tires, lights, horn, mirrors, exhaust, and windshield. Cost is typically $35 at authorized inspection stations.
washington-dc.registrationNotes: DC charges registration fees based on vehicle weight, ranging from $72 to $155 for most passenger vehicles. A 6% excise tax applies to vehicle purchases. Parking permits are required for on-street parking in most neighborhoods.
washington-dc.description: Washington DC has some of the most comprehensive vehicle ownership regulations in the nation. As the nation's capital, DC requires liability insurance, annual vehicle inspections, and offers generous incentives for electric vehicle adoption as part of its sustainability goals.
